news.title: Ireland’s international education sector risks hitting “social license wall”
news.summary_en: Housing pressures, perceptions of racism and concerns over graduate outcomes risk undermining public support for international students, panellists at the second edition of The PIE Live Ireland have warned.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Firmli plans AI co-pilot for international student recruitment
news.summary_en: The Norwegian company’s planned November launch will bring together student applications and communications to help recruitment teams identify issues requiring attention.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Overseas student commencements fall 5% in Australian higher education
news.summary_en: International student commencements at Australian higher education providers fell by almost 5% year-on-year in the first part of 2026, according to new preliminary government data.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: International graduates deliver $1.7tn lifetime boost to host economies
news.summary_en: International students who graduated in 2024 are projected to contribute USD $1.7 trillion to their host economies over their working lives, according to new global research seeking to put a price on their post-study impact.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: CPT crackdown threatens America’s student appeal
news.summary_en: As internship and work authorisations come under threat in the US, experts warn the Trump administration is upending the American pitch to international students.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Ireland’s international education challenge is access, not demand
news.summary_en: As visa uncertainty clouds a growing sector, Irish education leaders warn that bureaucracy and inconsistent decisions could weaken the country’s appeal to global students.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Pakistani graduate’s death puts alleged US study fraud in national spotlight
news.summary_en: The death of Pakistani graduate Laiba Aijaz has prompted intervention from the country’s Prime Minister amid allegations that her family was defrauded of millions of rupees by a man promising to secure her admission to Harvard University.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: ITECA warns Australian policy is “choking” international education and skills pipeline
news.summary_en: Australia’s independent tertiary education sector has accused the government of putting international education and the country’s long-term skills pipeline at risk, as providers grapple with rising costs and tighter policy settings.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: The PIE Live Ireland – live feed
news.summary_en: Follow along here for live updates from the conference.
news.author: The PIE News team

news.title: International security and defence: Is it time for universities to step up?
news.summary_en: In her latest column for The PIE, Diana Beech asks whether universities can keep their doors open to the world while guarding against growing security threats – and why getting that balance right has never mattered more.
news.author: Diana Beech

news.title: Curtin vows to fight WA mega-university merger
news.summary_en: Curtin University has vowed to “vigorously oppose” plans to merge three of Western Australia’s biggest universities, warning the proposed mega-institution would bring “cost, waste and loss of choice”.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: TrustEd framework and consistent visa process should enhance Ireland’s position
news.summary_en: Ireland remains well placed to attract international students, but uncertainty over visas and the implementation of new quality standards could shape its ability to capitalise on that demand, according to speakers preparing for The PIE Live Ireland.
news.author: Amy Baker
